AZ-900 measures foundational knowledge of cloud concepts and Azure services. Skills measured (from the official study guide):

  • Describe cloud concepts: 25–30%
  • Describe Azure architecture and services: 35–40%
  • Describe Azure management and governance: 30–35%

Microsoft updates its study guides regularly — check the official guide before your exam.

Deployment models: public, private and hybrid cloud (plus multi-cloud).

Service types and the shared responsibility model:

  • IaaS — you manage the OS, apps and data (e.g. Azure Virtual Machines)
  • PaaS — Azure manages the platform; you manage apps and data (e.g. Azure App Service)
  • SaaS — the provider runs the whole application (e.g. Microsoft 365)

Benefits: high availability, scalability, elasticity, reliability, predictability, security, governance and manageability. The consumption-based model turns CapEx into OpEx.

• Regions and region pairs; availability zones are physically separate data centers within a region
  • Hierarchy: management groups → subscriptions → resource groups → resources
  • Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is the deployment and management layer

• Compute: Virtual Machines, VM Scale Sets, Azure Virtual Desktop, containers (ACI, AKS), Azure Functions (serverless), App Service
  • Networking: Virtual Network, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute (private connection), Azure DNS
  • Storage: Blob, Files, Queues, Tables, Disks; redundancy options LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS; access tiers Hot, Cool, Cold, Archive
  • Identity: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), MFA, Conditional Access, Zero Trust and defense-in-depth

• Cost: Pricing calculator, TCO calculator, Microsoft Cost Management, tags
  • Governance: Azure Policy, resource locks, Microsoft Purview, Service Trust Portal
  • Management tools: Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, Azure Arc, ARM templates/Bicep
  • Monitoring: Azure Advisor, Azure Service Health, Azure Monitor (Log Analytics, alerts, Application Insights)
